title: Nightly improvements begin
items: Gear Scout now gets a nightly improvement session (about 1:40 AM): it reviews the day's logs and results, fixes what it finds, adds improvements, and notes them here.
Emails no longer say '⚠️ N source errors' for sites that always block automated access (Guitar Center, Sweetwater, Gearspace) or for eBay pausing at its daily limit — only real failures are flagged.
Facebook sold/pending checks wait only as long as each page needs instead of a fixed 2 seconds, so the hourly check finishes sooner.

title: B-stock value and 'Worth it only'
items: Each model now gets a B-stock value: what a dealer B-stock / open-box unit goes for (Reverb B-stock listings, or 85% of the new price). Cards show 'B-stock ~$X'.
New 'Worth it only' switch on the Dashboard and search: only listings at least 10% under B-stock value (or under the used value for vintage gear with no B-stock version).
Comps learn from you: hiding a listing Gear Scout called a deal or 'worth it' disputes its comp; after two, the comp is re-checked from scratch and shown as a rough estimate until then.
Sold comps: once Gear Scout has watched a model sell 3+ times, what it actually went for becomes that model's comp ('sold ~$X').
Mixed-price check: if a model's prices are all over the place (vintage and reissue mixed together), its comp isn't trusted for deals or 'worth it'.
Header: navigation has its own row with more space; labels no longer break mid-word.
Telex only shows listings at least 10% under the used price on Reverb (cards show 'Reverb used ~$X · N% under'); ones without a reliable Reverb price are in a collapsed group under each term.
Specific Telex terms ('Avalon 737', 'Distressor', 'Apollo X8P') get their own Reverb price, used for same-brand listings that don't name a model.
Facebook pictures are saved locally while their links work (Facebook links expire), so they keep showing; any picture that still fails shows a clean placeholder.
eBay pauses itself until the daily reset when its daily request allowance is used up; Telex buttons react instantly.

Every Telex listing gets a comp when at all possible: what the model sold for, its Reverb/eBay used price, Gear Scout's own price history (incl. sold listings), the Telex term's price, or similar past listings (est.). The card says which. Listings still without one are looked up first on each hourly refresh.

Dashboard only shows listings at least 10% under their comp (B-stock value when known, otherwise sold / Reverb-eBay used / history / similar listings) — no checkbox; listings without a comp are in one collapsed group at the bottom.

The 10%-under-comp rule applies everywhere: Dashboard, Deals, Telex, FB Posts, the email digests and the Facebook roundup (each listing shows its comp). Search, Lowest Price and favorites still show everything you asked for.
New-lowest-price alerts for every Telex term: a phone push (ntfy) + email when a listing comes in below the lowest price currently listed for that term across all sources.

title: Picked for you = real deals; cleaner Deals
items: Picked for you now only shows gear like your favorites that is 20%+ under a solid market value and within your usual price range (learned from your favorites), best deals first.
Deals need 30%+ under typical (40%+ under Reverb/eBay asking); anything over 85% under is treated as a mismatch, not a deal.
Tubes, tube sets, power supplies, transformers, meter bridges, capsules and other parts are valued as parts and never shown as deals.
Model versions are kept apart: AKG C12 VR vs. vintage C12, C414 XLS vs. XLII, U87 Ai, Mk II, reissues.
Bare model numbers after a brand are recognized (Universal Audio 1176, Neve 1073).
Telex and Lowest Price leave out pedal and plugin versions (UAFX LA-2A pedal, UAD plugins) unless your term asks for them, e.g. 'LA-2A pedal'.

Telex recognizes Universal Audio pedals sold without the word 'pedal' (LA-2A / 1176 'Studio Compressor', Lion '68…) and UA plugin versions of other makers' gear, and leaves out parts, add-ons and anything priced far below what the model sells for.
Telex shows every matching listing still for sale (not just recent ones or the cheapest 60): first 24 on screen, 'Show all' for the rest. Listings are kept 90 days instead of 30.

Air/HVAC compressors (tons, horsepower, R22, Trane, Campbell Hausfeld, Sears…) and consumer speakers (Bluetooth, car audio, PA systems, bookshelf/hi-fi) are filtered out; broad-word matches now need a pro brand or vintage clues, not just a $200+ price.

title: Faster everywhere
items: Reverb now comes through Reverb's data feed instead of a full browser: about 9 seconds instead of 25, and it sees every listing from the last 3 hours instead of just the first page.
Facebook groups are read more briefly on hourly refreshes and stop as soon as there's nothing new.
Dealer stores (Alto, Rudy's, Long & McQuade) are read every 3 hours on hourly refreshes — their stock changes slowly. Full scheduled runs still read them every time.
Market-price lookups run three at a time, and the hourly sold/pending checks run alongside them instead of after — the hourly refresh finishes in about half the time.
Pages open faster: the database got indexes for the lookups every page makes, and the dashboard pre-calculates prices and learning data in the background.
Sold/pending checks run several at a time, with Facebook checked alongside — the hourly check went from about 9 minutes to a couple.

title: Cleaner results, eBay, Telex
items: eBay connected: in scrapes, live search, Lowest Price (cheapest first), market values and Telex searches.
Broad search words (mic, condenser, preamp…) only count when a listing looks like studio gear: a pro brand, vintage clues, or $200+.
Filtered out: toys, karaoke, video games, ham radio, tapes/records, home-stereo gear, wireless mic systems, and accessory-only listings (setting).
Telex: cheapest first, eBay included, 'Search all terms now' and per-term 'Search everywhere' buttons with progress.
Facebook 'Pending' listings tracked and badged; pending items aren't counted as deals.
Dashboard: one section per site with a jump bar; a small site tag on every listing.

title: Smarter comps and learning
items: Comp prices compare like with like: brands recognized anywhere in the title, pedal/plugin/kit/500-series versions valued separately, bundles and parts handled.
Learning: how fast each model sells and what it went for, offer hints on listings up 3+ weeks, and Facebook post search that spends its time on terms that find posts.
